newsitem.title: FRANCE: French CFDT union blasts Shell plan.
newsitem.headline: French CFDT union blasts Shell plan.

text.p: The Socialist-led CFDT union took aim on Saturday at Royal Dutch/Shell group's plan to reduce capacity at its Berre refinery in southeast France.

"The CFDT deplores the lack of coordination with the unions and the lack of cooperation in the industry that leads to reducing production capacity rather than adapting it to demand," it said in a statement.

Shell France said on Saturday it would seek formal approval from the French industry ministry to reduce crude throughput at Berre to 3.5 million tonnes per year from 6.5 million tonnes and take one of its two catcrackers out of operation.

"The reduction of production capacity is not justified unless it is compensated by an increase in capacity for diesel production in which French refinery capacity is insufficient," the CFDT said. It said it would lobby French authorities with the aim of getting Shell to change its plan.
"In fact, the CFDT notes an improvement in margins in 1996 and reaffirms that there isn't global overcapacity," it said.
Shell said in December it was in talks with competitors operating in the area on plans to cooperate in cutting capacity.
European refiners last year announced closures, mergers or cutbacks at plants in Switzerland, Denmark, Germany, Britain and the Netherlands after profit margins slumped in 1995.
A Shell spokeswoman said on Saturday that it was premature to give any figure on job cuts resulting from the plan. She said the Berre refinery employs around 2,000 people.
